Huber+Suhner.why: makes optical circuit switches (OCS) in volume for a US hyperscaler's AI data-center network and passive fiber connectivity; OCS output is the main driver of its 2026 growth guidance
Huber+Suhner.evidence: Huber+Suhner Q2 FY2026 call (08-18-2026): CEO - OCS ramp-up with the first hyperscaler customer; order backlog from the U.S. hyperscaler OCS orders reaches mainly into next year; automated OCS production lines in Poland operational

players.product: POLATIS optical circuit switches (OCS) for hyperscale data-center networks, plus passive fiber connectivity / fiber management systems and WDM transceiver components (Cube Optics)

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 results: order intake CHF 543 million (CFO), organic growth 8.5%, reported +5.1% after FX (-4.5%) and copper (+1%); net sales CHF 457 million, +2.6% reported and 6% organic; EBIT CHF 41 million, 9% margin, down 110 basis points due to the OCS ramp-up; gross margin 36.6%; R&D CHF 32.6 million (7.1% of sales). CEO: third semester in a row with order intake above CHF 500 million, and this one barely includes U.S. hyperscaler orders.
quarterly_data.figure: order intake CHF 543 million (organic 8.5%, reported 5.1%); net sales CHF 457 million (+2.6%, organic 6%); EBIT CHF 41 million (9%)

quarterly_data.signal: Record order backlog of CHF 517 million at end of June 2026 (end of 2025: CHF 432 million), driven by positive book-to-bill in all three segments. CEO: the OCS backlog from the U.S. hyperscaler orders booked between June and August 2025 reaches clearly into this year and mainly into next year, as very little of it has been executed and shipped, so net sales lag orders; those orders triggered the investment to move OCS from high-mix small-batch to high-volume manufacturing.
quarterly_data.figure: order backlog CHF 517 million (end-2025 CHF 432 million)

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance confirmed for FY2026: organic sales growth of at least 10% and an EBIT margin in the upper half of the long-term objective of 10.5% to 12%; INGUN not included. CEO: good start into Q3; the step from 6% organic growth after six months to the promised 10% will largely have to come from the ramped-up OCS business, plus the industry ramp-up; it 'remains to be delivered' and depends on whether supplier bottlenecks arise, so the guidance is not narrowed.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 organic sales growth at least 10%; EBIT margin upper half of 10.5%-12%

quarterly_data.signal: OCS ramp-up (CEO): higher-automated production lines in Poland have been commissioned and are operational and production capacity has seen a major increase through automation; the ramp-up is on track, in the middle between internal slow and fast scenarios (number and timing of lines not disclosed). The intense collaboration with the first hyperscaler customer to mature the product for a productive hyperscaler network has been completed; demand is stable 'and if at all change, then more up than down'; output in H2 is expected to clearly increase versus H1.

CEO on further OCS customers: Huber+Suhner has contacts with a broad range of other customers, among them other hyperscalers that are less advanced in deploying OCS in their architecture but are testing this kind of equipment, including Huber+Suhner's; no timeline can be given for additional hyperscaler orders. OCS will be used in both AI training and inference, 'but the lion share of the volume will be in productive networks'.

Communication segment slipped to a negative EBIT margin in H1 2026 (EBIT CHF 13 million lower than H1 2025) because of OCS ramp-up and pre-investment costs and lower mobile and fixed-network demand. CEO: OCS is expected to become accretive in H2 2026; with a completed OCS ramp-up the communication segment is planned to deliver double-digit EBIT margins midterm. The non-data-center communications business (about CHF 120 million per semester) is believed to have reached the bottom.

CEO on the data-center market: it still benefits from AI build-outs and is not yet peaking; large hyperscalers' investment plans 'are ever going up' and investments are further accelerating. Huber+Suhner serves it through passive connectivity including its fiber management system and through OCS; its components business also sells WDM components from Cube Optics and RF connectors into data-center transceivers.

CEO on the optical fiber shortage: it affects the whole industry, driven by AI data-center demand and by basic materials for fiber production stuck in the Strait of Hormuz; Huber+Suhner, a small consumer of fiber, has not been affected so far, is planning ahead and does not expect to be severely affected.

Industry segment H1 2026: record order intake CHF 242 million (+42%), net sales CHF 189 million (+22%), operating profit CHF 37 million or 19.6% margin, driven by aerospace & defense and test & measurement; CEO: test & measurement demand is driven by electronics penetration and by testing of equipment that goes into AI data centers. Transportation order intake CHF 161 million.
quarterly_data.figure: industry order intake CHF 242 million (+42%); sales CHF 189 million (+22%); margin 19.6%

quarterly_data.signal: Cash flow and investment: H1 2026 capex CHF 28 million (roughly 6% of sales); free cash flow from operating activities CHF 3 million (H1 2025: CHF 63 million) and free operating cash flow minus CHF 25 million, mainly due to inventory build-up for the OCS ramp-up and aerospace & defense.
quarterly_data.figure: capex CHF 28 million; free operating cash flow minus CHF 25 million

quarterly_data.signal: Acquisition of INGUN (Konstanz, Germany; high-precision test pins for RF and electrical contact testing): a bit over 400 people, production in Germany and Vietnam, 2025 sales in the high double-digit million franc range; closing planned towards the end of Q3 2026, contributing from Q4 2026 and not included in the guidance.
